newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission targets solvents' air pollution role.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission targets solvents' air pollution role.

text.p: European Union countries will have to cut by two-thirds emissions of solvents used to make paints, varnishes and other products so as to reduce their air pollution effects, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

The proposals, which have to go before the 15 EU member countries and the European Parliament, will not come into full force before 2007, when solvent vapour emissions must be cut to 700,000 tonnes a year compared with a projected figure of 2.2 million.
"To reach this goal, the Commission leaves member states the choice between two different options for action," the EU executive said in a statement.
Countries could either follow EU-set emission limit values for their industries to meet as they think fit or they could design national plans tailored to their own industries.

"The reduction of releases of these substances is imperative since they cause, together with nitrogen oxides and sunlight, summer smog...a highly toxic and irritating gas," the Commission said in a news statement.
Summer smogs during Europe's recent warm, dry summers have been blamed for a variety of effects including increased deaths among the elderly or people with damaged lungs.
Pollution incidents, sparked mainly by emissions from road transport, industry and power stations, also cause breathing difficulties for asthma sufferers and damage to crops and buildings.
Certain solvent vapours themselves cause cancer and can affect reproduction, the statement said.
Twenty industrial sectors would be hit by the proposals, the statement said, though it failed to name them.
Proposed changes would require industries to shift to new technologies and develop new techniques for activities such as coating and cleaning, it said.
